description: INRAE’s Réal Collobrier observatory records rainfall, streamflow and other hydroclimatic measurements in ten nested forested catchments in the Maures massif, southeast France. The Data in Brief article reports outlet flows from basins of 1.57–70 square kilometres, fifteen rain gauges, water temperature and soil observations, with a series extending from 1967 to 2024. Soil-moisture measurements at several depths began in 2019. The Recherche Data Gouv version 2 copy lists nine public files, including separate archives for discharge, rain, climatology, conductivity, soil humidity and water temperature, under Etalab Open Licence 2.0. Coverage is one Mediterranean catchment system, not a national river network or direct observations of engineered drainage assets. Known limitations include intermittent streams, gaps and homogenisation procedures described by the article, and a much shorter soil-moisture span than the flow series. A reviewer-assessed use is calibrating catchment runoff or drought-response components in flood and water-supply scenarios. model-wflow is a related hydrological simulator, but no import or calibration was attempted. The alternative BDOH portal requires a free account for downloads; the public repository copy has no restricted files. No archive was downloaded.
